record.title: Kyrgyzstan China-frontier COVID closure order and phased cargo restoration
record.scope: Land frontier with China; Torugart and Irkeshtam
record.movement: China-frontier travellers and road freight, subject to exceptions and staged restoration
record.exceptions: February 3 summary includes diplomats, returning citizens and specified freight drivers; April restoration cargo-only. Official April 2 guidance specifically exempts humanitarian cargo at the China frontier.
record.imposing_authority: Kyrgyzstan government; bilateral implementation arrangements with China
record.enforcement: Formal government closure announcement; later Kyrgyz MFA cargo-restoration reports.
record.relationship: Earlier China-specific frontier phase linked to national Kyrgyz regime CC011; neither independent national decision nor duplicate of March 19 foreign-entry ban.
record.status_observation: April 14 Irkeshtam freight restoration was agreed/reported; a May 22 ministry table counts resumed arrivals from April 16. June 8 Torugart freight restoration was only announced in the reviewed June 3 report. No full or first-passage reopening date is established.
record.official_rationale: Kyrgyz government cited preventing coronavirus entry.
record.context: Frontier-specific decision preceded Kyrgyzstan’s March national foreign-entry restriction.
record.uncertainty: Formal February 1 decision is not a claim of the first physical closure. Earlier January restriction and New Year shutdown overlap. Kabar and 24.kg rely on the same MFA lineage; April 14 is partial restoration, not complete frontier reopening. A May 22 ministry operational table counts resumed Irkeshtam arrivals from April 16; April 14 remains a diplomatic/reporting endpoint, not independently verified first vehicle passage.

historical.duration_note: No supported continuous operational interval for the stated scope. No measured continuous interval is established.

claim_checks.Historical note — current findings are i: Government decision and subsequent restoration accounts establish the restriction.
February 1 is formal decision day; operational accounts differ January 23/February 2.
April 14 is freight-restoration agreement/reporting date for Irkeshtam. A May 22 ministry table counts resumed arrivals from April 16; first exceptional passage and full reopening remain unproved.

Hierarchical coding: see Rationale coding for subcategories, attribution and phases. The recorded rationale and claim assessment support the selected subcategories. All applicable broad categories are retained together; no primary rationale is imposed. Prior evidence assessment (before this recoding): Government invokes coronavirus prevention.
Crossing and category phases differ; April 2 official guidance expressly exempts humanitarian cargo at China frontier. General later-decree exemptions are not proof of unrestricted freight there.
Different start definitions, exemptions and crossing-specific restarts preclude a single duration.
